title: NDA 2 2026: 394 Vacancies, Exam 13 Sep, Apply by 9 Jun
meta_description: NDA 2 2026: 394 vacancies (370 male, 24 female) for Army, Navy, Air Force wings. Exam 13 Sep 2026. Apply 20 May-9 Jun. Age 16.5-19.5. Class 12 PCM required.

hero.one_liner: Gateway to Indian Armed Forces as an officer - join Army, Navy, or Air Force through India's premier defence training academy after 12th

what_is_it: The National Defence Academy (NDA) exam is conducted by UPSC twice a year (NDA I and NDA II) to recruit candidates for the NDA and Naval Academy courses. NDA is the premier tri-service training academy located in Khadakwasla, Pune, where cadets are trained for 3 years before being commissioned as officers in the Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force.

The exam is open to 12th pass or appearing candidates aged 16.5-19.5 years. For Army wing, any stream (Arts/Science/Commerce) works. For Navy and Air Force, 12th with Physics and Mathematics is mandatory. After clearing the written exam (conducted by UPSC), candidates appear for SSB Interview (5-day assessment) which tests personality, officer-like qualities, and leadership potential.

NDA is considered one of the most prestigious career paths for young Indians. Officers commissioned through NDA are highly respected and receive excellent training, salary, and perks. Starting salary after training is approximately ₹56,100 basic + allowances = ₹70,000-90,000/month, with free accommodation, medical, canteen, and other facilities.
NDA I 2026 exam is scheduled for 13 April 2026. The notification is typically released 3-4 months before the exam date.

extra_sections.heading: SSB Interview - The Real Challenge
content: The SSB (Services Selection Board) Interview is a 5-day assessment that tests whether you have 'Officer Like Qualities (OLQs)'. It's not a traditional interview - it's a comprehensive personality assessment conducted by psychologists and military officers.
Day 1 - Screening: Officer Intelligence Rating (OIR) test + Picture Perception and Description Test (PPDT) + group discussion on the story you wrote. About 50-60% are screened out on Day 1.

Day 2 - Psychology Tests: Thematic Apperception Test (TAT - write stories on pictures), Word Association Test (WAT - write sentences for 60 words in 15 seconds each), Situation Reaction Test (SRT - respond to 60 situations), and Self Description Test (SD).

Day 3 & 4 - Group Testing Officer (GTO) tasks: Group Discussion, Group Planning Exercise, Progressive Group Task, Half Group Task, Individual Obstacles, Command Task, and Final Group Task. These are outdoor activities testing leadership, teamwork, and problem-solving.
Day 5 - Personal Interview with the Interviewing Officer (IO). Questions about your background, interests, family, current affairs, and motivation for joining defence forces.
Conference with all three assessors - final recommendation.
About 1 in 6-8 candidates who appear for SSB get recommended. SSB preparation is as important as written exam preparation.
Read 'Let's Crack SSB Interview' by Dr. Arth Chopra for comprehensive guidance.

extra_sections.heading: NDA Scoring Strategy & Cutoff
content: NDA written exam has 2 papers: Mathematics (300 marks, 120 questions) and GAT (600 marks, 150 questions). Total: 900 marks.
SSB Interview adds 900 marks, making the final merit out of 1800.
Written exam cutoff for General category typically ranges from 340-370 marks (out of 900). This means you need approximately 38-41% to clear the written stage.
However, the SSB interview rejection rate is 85-90%, so clearing the written exam is just the beginning.
The safest strategy: aim for 180+ in Mathematics and 200+ in GAT. Mathematics is the differentiator - most candidates score similarly in GAT, but strong math performance creates a comfortable buffer.
Focus on Calculus, Matrices, and Trigonometry which together carry 100+ marks.

extra_sections.heading: NDA vs CDS vs Agnipath - Which Path to Choose?
NDA - the fastest path to officer rank
content: NDA (National Defence Academy) is India's premier tri-service training academy in Khadakwasla, Pune. Cadets join after 12th class (age 16.5-19.5) and undergo 3 years of training + 1 year at their respective service academy (IMA/INA/AFA).
Upon graduation, they're commissioned as Lieutenant with immediate officer status.

NDA is the fastest and youngest entry into officer rank - you become a Lieutenant at age 22-23, while CDS (Combined Defence Services) graduates become officers at 25-26 and AFCAT officers at 24-25. The early start compounds over your career - NDA officers typically retire at higher ranks than later-entry officers.

The training is holistic - academic degree (BA/BSc/BCom from Jawaharlal Nehru University), physical training, military training, adventure activities, and character building. NDA graduates form the backbone of India's military leadership - the bond and network formed here lasts a lifetime.

extra_sections.heading: NDA salary and benefits
extra_sections.content:
Starting salary (Lieutenant): Rs 56,100 basic + Military Service Pay Rs 15,500 + DA. Total monthly: Rs 85,000-1,00,000.

Free accommodation, medical for entire family, canteen facilities, subsidized rations, and 60 days annual leave. After 20 years of service: pension for life.

The non-monetary benefits (respect, adventure, travel, leadership experience) are unmatched.

extra_sections.heading: SSB interview - the real filter
extra_sections.content:
The written exam shortlists 5-6x the vacancies. SSB (Services Selection Board) interview is the real selection - only 10-15% clear it.

The 5-day assessment tests OLQs (Officer Like Qualities): initiative, determination, courage, group planning, and communication. You can't fake it - SSB tests your natural personality.

Start group discussions, sports, and leadership activities NOW to develop these traits naturally.

extra_sections.heading: NDA written exam - detailed section strategy
content: Mathematics (300 marks): This paper covers Class 11-12 level math - Algebra (quadratic equations, complex numbers, permutation-combination, binomial theorem), Matrices and Determinants, Trigonometry (identities, inverse functions, height and distance), Analytical Geometry (2D and 3D), Differential Calculus (limits, continuity, differentiation, maxima-minima), Integral Calculus (integration methods, definite integrals, area under curves), Vector Algebra, and Statistics and Probability.
The math paper is what separates NDA from other defense exams. If you're strong in Class 11-12 math, you have a significant advantage.

Arts stream students often struggle here - if math is your weakness, start preparation from Class 11 NCERT and build up gradually. RS Aggarwal NDA Mathematics and Pathfinder NDA by Arihant are the standard books.
Focus on Trigonometry and Calculus - they carry approximately 100 marks combined (33% of the paper). Master the 20 most common trigonometric identities and the 10 standard integration formulas.
These formulas appear in some form in every single NDA paper. Create a formula sheet and revise it daily for the last 2 months.
GAT - General Ability Test (600 marks): Divided into English (200 marks) and General Knowledge (400 marks). English tests comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, and usage through MCQs.
GK covers Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Indian History, Geography, Current Affairs, and General Science.

extra_sections.heading: SSB interview - the 5-day assessment
content: Day 1 - Screening: Officer Intelligence Rating (OIR) test - verbal and non-verbal reasoning MCQs. Picture Perception and Description Test (PPDT) - you're shown a hazy picture for 30 seconds, write a story around it in 4 minutes, then narrate it to your group and participate in group discussion.
Approximately 50-60% of candidates are screened out on Day 1.

Day 2 - Psychology Tests: Thematic Apperception Test (TAT) - write stories for 12 pictures in 4 minutes each. Word Association Test (WAT) - write a sentence for each of 60 words shown for 15 seconds each.
Situation Reaction Test (SRT) - write your reaction to 60 situations in 30 minutes. Self Description Test (SD) - describe how your parents, teachers, and friends see you.
These tests assess your personality traits - initiative, courage, determination, social adaptability, and group effectiveness.

Days 3-4 - Group Testing: Group Discussion (GD) on current topics, Group Planning Exercise (GPE) - analyze a problem scenario and devise a group plan, Progressive Group Task (PGT) - physical outdoor tasks completed as a group, Half Group Task (HGT) - same as PGT with half the group, Individual Obstacles - cross 10 physical obstacles individually (rope climbing, jumping, balancing), Command Task - you lead a small group through a physical task, Final Group Task (FGT) - last group exercise.

Day 5 - Personal Interview: 30-45 minute interview with the Interviewing Officer. Covers personal history, family background, education, hobbies, current affairs, defense knowledge, and situational questions.
The IO probes your motivations for joining defense and assesses your personality consistency with psychology test results.

SSB success rate: Only 10-15% of screened-in candidates (who clear Day 1) receive final recommendation. The key is consistency - your psychology tests, group behavior, and interview should all reflect the same personality.
Trying to 'perform' or 'fake' Officer Like Qualities is the fastest way to get rejected. Be genuine, show initiative, stay calm under pressure, and demonstrate team spirit.

extra_sections.heading: NDA training - 3 years at the academy
content: NDA (Khadakwasla, Pune) training spans 6 semesters over 3 years. Cadets pursue a BA/BSc/BCom degree from Jawaharlal Nehru University simultaneously with military training.

The academic curriculum includes subjects relevant to your chosen service - Army cadets study military history and strategy, Navy cadets study navigation and marine engineering, Air Force cadets study aerodynamics and aviation.

Physical training is intense and progressive: morning PT at 5:30 AM (running, swimming, cross-country, assault course), followed by drill, weapon training, map reading, field craft, and tactical exercises. Swimming is mandatory - you must pass a swimming test in the first term.
Non-swimmers receive compulsory swimming coaching.

The famous NDA traditions: inter-squadron competitions in sports, debates, and cultural events build camaraderie and competitive spirit. The passing out parade at the end of 3 years is attended by the President or Defense Minister.
NDA friendships last a lifetime - the bond formed through shared physical and mental challenges during training is unlike anything in civilian life.
After NDA: Army cadets go to Indian Military Academy (IMA, Dehradun) for 1 year. Navy cadets go to Indian Naval Academy (INA, Ezhimala) for 1 year.

Air Force cadets go to Air Force Academy (AFA, Dundigal) for 1.5 years. Upon successful completion, you're commissioned as a Lieutenant (Army), Sub-Lieutenant (Navy), or Flying Officer (Air Force) with full officer status and permanent commission.
For more details, see our guide on SSC GD Constable 2026.

extra_sections.heading: NDA preparation - 6 month plan for Class 11-12 students
content: Month 1-2 (Math foundation): Complete Class 11 math from NCERT - Algebra, Trigonometry, Coordinate Geometry, Statistics. Solve RS Aggarwal NDA Mathematics chapter-wise.
Simultaneously start reading newspaper daily for GK and English improvement. Begin light physical training - running 2km, pushups, pullups.
Month 3-4 (GK + English depth): Complete Class 12 math (Calculus, Vectors, Probability). Start GK preparation - NCERT History Class 6-12, Geography Class 6-12, Science Class 9-10.
Practice English grammar from Wren & Martin. Increase physical training - 5km runs, swimming practice, obstacle course at local army coaching.
Month 5 (Mock tests): Take 2 full-length NDA mocks per week. Analyze math paper mistakes - identify topics where you consistently lose marks.
Revise GK notes weekly. Practice English comprehension passages daily.
Physical fitness should be at SSB standard - 2.4km run under 12 minutes, 10+ pullups, 30+ pushups.
Month 6 (Final revision): Take 1 mock daily in the last 2 weeks. Revise math formula sheet every morning.
Revise 6-month current affairs compilation. Practice PPDT (Picture Perception and Description Test) with friends - this is the Day 1 screening test at SSB.
Sleep well, eat well, and maintain your physical fitness - SSB is physically and mentally demanding.

extra_sections.heading: NDA vs CDS vs AFCAT - which defense entry to choose
content: NDA (after 12th, age 16.5-19.5): The youngest and most prestigious entry. 3 years at NDA + 1 year at service academy = 4 years of training.
You graduate as a degree holder with a permanent commission.
The long training period builds the strongest military foundation. Best for students who are certain about a military career from school.
CDS (after graduation, age 19-25): Combined Defence Services exam by UPSC. Shorter training - 18 months at IMA (Army), 1 year at INA (Navy), or 1.5 years at AFA (Air Force).
Faster entry into service but you miss the NDA bonding experience. Best for graduates who discovered their interest in defense later.
CDS officers and NDA officers serve together at equal rank after commissioning.
AFCAT (after graduation, age 20-26): Air Force Common Admission Test. Only for Air Force - flying, navigation, and ground duty branches.
Shorter training (1.5 years at AFA). Best for graduates specifically interested in the Air Force who don't want to wait for CDS results.
AFCAT has a separate technical entry for engineering graduates.
Territorial Army (after graduation, working professionals): Part-time military service - you serve in the Army for 2-3 months per year while maintaining your civilian career. No full-time commitment.
Great option for working professionals who want military experience without leaving their jobs. Officers earn military salary during attachment period in addition to their civilian income.

If you're currently in Class 11-12 and interested in defense, NDA is the unambiguous best choice. You enter at the youngest age, get the most comprehensive training, and build the longest career in uniform.
Every year you delay is a year of seniority you lose compared to NDA batchmates.

extra_sections.heading: Life as an NDA officer - career and lifestyle
content: Career progression in the Army: Lieutenant (commissioning) → Captain (after 2 years) → Major (after 6 years cumulative) → Lieutenant Colonel (after 13 years) → Colonel (selection-based) → Brigadier → Major General → Lieutenant General → General. NDA officers frequently reach Colonel rank by age 40-42 due to their early entry advantage.

Salary progression: Lieutenant Rs 56,100 basic → Captain Rs 61,300 → Major Rs 69,400 → Lt Colonel Rs 1,21,200 → Colonel Rs 1,30,600 → Brigadier Rs 1,39,600. With Military Service Pay (Rs 15,500), DA, and allowances, a Colonel earns approximately Rs 2.5-3 lakh/month.
Plus free accommodation (bungalow in cantonment), medical for life, canteen facilities, and pension after 20 years of service.

Posting variety: You serve across India - from Siachen Glacier to Andaman Islands, from Rajasthan deserts to Northeast jungles. Postings rotate every 2-3 years - peace stations (Pune, Dehradun, Mhow) alternate with field areas (Kashmir, Northeast, border areas).
Some officers serve in UN peacekeeping missions abroad (Congo, South Sudan, Lebanon) - international exposure with UN daily allowance in dollars.

The intangible rewards: Commanding 120 soldiers at age 24 (Company Commander), leading a battalion of 800 at age 38, making decisions that affect lives - these leadership experiences are impossible to replicate in any civilian career. The discipline, fitness, and resilience you develop become permanent personality traits.
NDA officers consistently rate among the most satisfied professionals in surveys despite the hardship postings.

Post-retirement career: Military officers retire between age 54-60 depending on rank. Post-retirement options include corporate security (Rs 15-30 LPA), defense consulting, strategic advisory roles, politics, farming on allotted land, coaching academy for NDA aspirants, or government advisory positions.
The discipline and leadership skills are highly valued in the corporate world.

extra_sections.heading: Physical fitness requirements and preparation
content: SSB physical standards: Height - minimum 157cm for Army, 157cm for Navy, 162.5cm for Air Force (male). For female candidates: 152cm minimum.
Weight proportional to height (BMI 18-25). Vision: 6/6 in better eye, 6/9 in worse eye without glasses for Army.
Air Force flying branch requires 6/6 in both eyes without glasses - LASIK is accepted if done 6 months prior.

Individual obstacles at SSB: You face 10 obstacles - rope climbing (6 meters), balance beam, Burma bridge, tiger leap (jumping across a gap), commando walk (rope traverse), and others. Each obstacle tests a different physical skill - upper body strength, balance, agility, and courage.
Practice at your local Army coaching center or gymnasium.
Physical preparation timeline: Start 6 months before the expected SSB date. Month 1-2: Build basic fitness - daily running (3km), 20 pushups, 5 pullups, 30 squats.

Month 3-4: Increase intensity - 5km runs under 25 minutes, 40 pushups, 10 pullups, obstacle practice. Month 5-6: Peak fitness - run 2.4km in under 10 minutes, 50 pushups, 15 pullups, all individual obstacles comfortable.
Swimming is mandatory: NDA training includes compulsory swimming. If you can't swim, learn now - join a local swimming class.
You need to swim 100 meters without stopping. At NDA, non-swimmers receive intensive coaching, but having basic swimming skills before joining reduces stress during the first term significantly.

extra_sections.heading: Books and coaching for NDA
content: Standard books: Pathfinder NDA/NA by Arihant (comprehensive - covers math, English, and GK in one book), RS Aggarwal NDA Mathematics (best for math practice), Lucent's General Knowledge (covers all GK topics), Wren and Martin English Grammar. These 4 books are sufficient for 95% of NDA preparation.
Don't buy more than 4-5 books - depth in fewer books beats surface-level coverage across many.
Free resources: NDA previous year papers with solutions are available on UPSC website (upsc.gov.in). NCERT textbooks (free PDFs at ncert.nic.in) cover 70% of the GK syllabus.
YouTube channels like Defence Guru, MKC, and SSBCrack offer free NDA preparation lectures and SSB guidance.

Coaching institutes: Centurion Defence Academy (Lucknow), Major Kalshi Classes (Allahabad), Shield Defence Academy (Delhi) are popular for NDA coaching. Fees range from Rs 30,000-80,000 for 6-12 month programs.

Online coaching (Unacademy NDA, Testbook Defence) costs Rs 5,000-15,000 and covers the same syllabus. Self-study works well for NDA if you're disciplined with NCERT textbooks and previous year papers.

extra_sections.text: NDA is the youngest entry into the Indian Armed Forces - cadets who clear it at 16-17 years of age retire as senior officers with a lifetime of service, honour, and one of the best pension packages in the country.

preparation_tips: Mathematics paper (300 marks) is the game-changer. If you're weak in Math, NDA will be very tough. Cover: Algebra, Matrices, Trigonometry, Calculus (basics), Analytical Geometry, Vector Algebra, Statistics, and Probability. Use NCERT 11th-12th Math textbooks as primary resource.

General Ability Test Paper 2 has two sections: English (200 marks) and General Knowledge (400 marks). GK covers Physics, Chemistry, Biology, History, Geography, Current Affairs, and Defence-related topics. Focus on NCERT 6-12 for science and social studies.

Start SSB preparation from Day 1 - don't wait till after the written exam. Read newspapers daily, develop opinions on national/international issues, practice group discussions with friends, and work on your physical fitness. SSB evaluates your personality over 5 days - it can't be faked.

Physical fitness is essential - not for the written exam but for SSB (obstacle course, outdoor tasks) and the 3-year NDA training which is very physically demanding. Start running, swimming, and body-weight exercises now. Target: 5 km run in under 25 minutes.

faqs.question: Can girls apply for NDA?
faqs.answer:
Yes. The Supreme Court ordered women's admission to NDA in 2021, and female candidates have been appearing since 2022.

Women can join the Army and Air Force wings through NDA. The training and curriculum are the same.

Women officers are fully commissioned with equal ranks and pay.

faqs.question: What degree do you get at NDA?
faqs.answer:
NDA cadets earn a Bachelor's degree from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) during their 3-year training. Army cadets get BA/BSc.

Navy and Air Force cadets get BSc. The degree is fully recognized and equivalent to any regular university degree.

faqs.question: What if I clear the written exam but fail SSB?
faqs.answer:
You can appear again in the next NDA exam cycle (NDA I or NDA II) as long as you meet the age criteria. Many successful NDA candidates clear SSB on their 2nd or 3rd attempt.

Each SSB attempt teaches you something and improves your chances. Retain your written exam result for analysis - understand what went wrong in SSB.

faqs.question: NDA salary after training?
faqs.answer: After 4 years of training (3 NDA + 1 academy), you're commissioned as Lieutenant at Level 10 - basic pay ₹56,100/month + DA + Military Service Pay + Transport Allowance + other allowances = approximately ₹80,000-90,000/month. Plus free accommodation in military cantonment, medical for family, canteen facilities, and subsidized education for children.

faqs.question: I'm 19 and in final year of graduation. NDA or CDS?
faqs.answer:
If you're below 19.5 years, you're still eligible for NDA. However, NDA means leaving college and starting 3-year training (you'll get a degree at NDA).

CDS allows you to complete your graduation first and then join for shorter training (1.5 years). If you value your current degree program, wait for CDS after graduation.

If you want the full NDA experience (most prestigious entry), apply immediately.

faqs.question: What is the pass rate for NDA?
faqs.answer:
Approximately 6-8% of written exam applicants make it to SSB. Of those who appear for SSB, about 15-20% get recommended.

Overall selection rate is roughly 1-2% of total applicants (200K+ apply, ~300-400 selected). It's competitive but achievable with focused preparation.

faqs.question: Can girls apply for NDA?
faqs.answer:
Yes, since 2022. Girls are eligible for NDA following the Supreme Court order.

They can join Army, Navy, and Air Force through NDA. Physical standards are different for female candidates.

The training at NDA is the same - no separate or easier syllabus. This is a historic change opening the youngest military entry to women.

faqs.question: What subjects are needed for NDA?
faqs.answer:
For Army wing: Any stream (Arts/Science/Commerce) in 12th. For Navy and Air Force: Must have Physics and Mathematics in 12th.

If you want to keep all three options open, take Science with Physics + Math in 11th-12th. The written exam has Mathematics paper (Class 12 level) regardless of which wing you apply for.

faqs.question: How to prepare for NDA written exam?
faqs.answer:
Mathematics (300 marks): Class 11-12 level - focus on algebra, trigonometry, calculus, vectors, and probability. Practice NCERT + Pathfinder NDA by Arihant.

GAT (600 marks): English (200) + GK (400). English: grammar, vocabulary, comprehension.

GK: physics, chemistry, history, geography, current affairs. Read NCERT Class 9-12 for science and social studies.
